title: Add `live` and `timezone` attributes to the <time> element
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

## Summary

I'd like to propose two new attributes for the existing `<time>` element: `live` and `timezone`. Together, they would allow developers to display a live, auto-updating clock in any timezone — without writing any JavaScript.

---

## The Problem

Displaying a live clock is one of the most common UI tasks on the web. Yet today, every developer has to write the same repetitive JavaScript to achieve it:

```javascript
function updateClock() {
  const now = new Date();
  const options = {
    timeZone: 'Asia/Karachi',
    hour: '2-digit',
    minute: '2-digit',
    second: '2-digit',
    hour12: true
  };
  document.getElementById('clock').textContent =
    new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', options).format(now);
}

setInterval(updateClock, 1000);
updateClock();
```

This is boilerplate. Every developer writes it. Every project repeats it. It should not require JavaScript at all.

---

## Proposed Solution

Extend the existing `<time>` element with two new attributes:

- `live` — makes the element auto-update every second
- `timezone="..."` — accepts any valid IANA timezone string

The same clock above would simply become:

```html
<time live timezone="Asia/Karachi"></time>
```

That's it. No JavaScript. No setInterval. No Intl.DateTimeFormat boilerplate.

---

## More Examples

```html
<!-- Pakistan Standard Time -->
<time live timezone="Asia/Karachi"></time>

<!-- New York -->
<time live timezone="America/New_York"></time>

<!-- London -->
<time live timezone="Europe/London"></time>

<!-- Local device time (no timezone attr) -->
<time live></time>
```

---

## Precedent in HTML

This pattern is not new — HTML has done this before:

- `<input type="date">` replaced JS datepicker libraries
- `<input type="color">` replaced JS color pickers
- `<video>` and `<audio>` replaced JS-based media players

A live clock is equally universal. It deserves the same treatment.

---

## Why Extend <time> and Not a New Tag?

The `<time>` element already exists for representing time-related content. These two attributes are a natural extension of what it already does — just making it live and timezone-aware. No new element needed.

---

## Open Questions

- Should `format` attribute also be supported for custom display formats?
- Should `live` accept an interval value like `live="1000"` (ms)?
- How should browsers handle this when JavaScript is disabled?

Open to all feedback and discussion. Thanks for considering this.
